# jochwacht-sbom 0.13.1 — your own older bill is yours again

Three defects from the rename of 01.10.2026, all of them measured against the
published 0.13.0 rather than inferred.

## A bill written by an earlier release was refused as somebody else's

The tool never overwrites a bill it did not write — that file is your
evidence. The check reads the `metadata.tools` stamp, and the set of names
this tool has signed its output with had collapsed to one. The effect on
0.13.0: a `sbom.cdx.json` written by 0.11.1 counted as foreign, the run
stopped with exit 1, and the message said your own file "was not written by
jochwacht-sbom". Without `--sbom PATH` you could not proceed.

Fixed, with the asymmetry that keeps it honest: **we write the current name
and read every name this tool ever wrote.** Both stamp layouts are read —
older bills carry `metadata.tools` as a list, newer ones as an object. A
genuinely foreign bill is still refused, unchanged.

## A declaration file under the former name was ignored in silence

If your project holds a hand-written dependency declaration under the
previous spelling, it is **not** read: one spelling per file, no
compatibility layer. That has not changed. What has changed is that the run
now says so:

```
Note: <former name> is present and is not read — this tool only reads
jochwacht-deps.yaml. Rename it (mv …) or its contents are left out of the bill.
```

Before this release the file was skipped without a word, so a declared
component simply disappeared from the bill. Rename the file and it is read as
before. The note informs, it does not gate.

## Wrong text in the release of 0.13.0

The 0.13.0 notes and the README described a migration path that does not
exist — forwarding commands, alias packages, and two `pipx uninstall` lines
that both named the *new* package. Following them would have removed the tool
you had just installed. The README now states the actual position: a clean
swap, no layer, every release under the earlier names withdrawn from PyPI.
The package summary no longer ends in a sentence that referred to itself.

## Nothing else changed

No scanner change, no new format, no new field. 206 tests, Linux and Windows,
Python 3.11 and 3.12.
